output.summary: A climbing or trailing herb native to the Afrotropics and Asia, hyacinth bean has three-part leaves and flattened pods containing several seeds. Its edible seeds are cultivated for food, while the pods contain high levels of cyanogenic glycosides and must be cooked carefully for human consumption.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are edible; pods contain high levels of cyanogenic glycosides and require careful cooking. In Piura, the beans commonly accompany ceviche.
